mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as required by destination jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, Luxembourg Freezing Notices issued by the Ministry of Finance, and national PEP databases. All directors, UBOs, signatories, and agents must undergo enhanced due diligence for PEP status, adverse media checks, sanctions screening, and negative news monitoring. Screening frequency and risk scoring must follow CSSF Circular 20/744 and Law of 12 November 2004, with escalation for any Politically Exposed Person or sanctioned entity identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers portal (lbr.lu) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in French, German, Luxembourgish, or in the Latin alphabet; foreign-language names require transliteration into the Latin alphabet. The name must be distinctive and not misleading. Where non-Latin characters are used in the original entity name, a standardized transliteration and a legal translation into French or German must be submitted. The RCS may refuse names contrary to Luxembourg public policy or requiring statutory authorization when the applicant has not obtained it.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the RCS issues a notice stating the grounds. The applicant may file a written appeal with the Minister of Justice via registered mail within 15 days of the rejection notice, attaching the RCS refusal letter and a revised name proposal. A name reservation may be extended by written request to the RCS before the expiry of the initial 30-day period. If the Minister of Justice affirmatively upholds the rejection, the applicant may contest the decision before the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within one month of notification, in accordance with Article 1034 of the Luxembourg Code of Civil Procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are not permissible as the statutory seat of an SCSp. A physical address in Luxembourg is required. A flexible office or co-working business center with a manned reception and registered-office services may satisfy the address requirement, provided the premises are a genuine physical location. A fully remote virtual office with no physical presence or mail handling in Luxembourg does not meet the statutory requirements of the Law of 10 June 2009 on commercial premises and EU substance expectations for pass-through partnership status.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annual probability for a standard low-risk surgical consumables manufacturing entity; increases to 25% if the registered office is a domiciliation service provider or if AML/CFT risk flags arise during onboarding.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 194-1 et seq. (Special Limited Partnership / SCSp), as introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013; Law of 16 May 2018 on dematerialised legal-entity formalities; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2015 on the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), acting through the eJust digital filing portal (https://www.lbr.lu; https://ejustice.public.lu)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited Partnership Agreement / Articles of Association (acte de société / contrat de société) filed with the RCS and published in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum. An SCSp is exempt from minimum capital requirements: paid-up capital is freely set in the partnership agreement, may be zero, and no bank escrow certificate or blocked-account rule applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF [SCSp] (the 'Partnership'), ADOPTED IN LIEU OF A MEETING, PURSUANT TO THE LUXEMBOURG LAW OF 10 AUGUST 1915 ON COMMERCIAL COMPANIES, AS AMENDED, AND ARTICLE [•] OF THE LIMITED PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT. 1. Subscription. The subscription schedule evidencing each founding limited partner's contributions is approved and adopted in full; no further capital calls are made at this stage. 2. Registered office. The registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, and the Registrar is instructed to file the relevant documentation. 3. Management. [Name] is appointed manager (gérant) of the Partnership, with authority to execute the suture-manufacturing business, open bank accounts, appoint accountants and legal counsel, and sign all statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS name reservation and availability check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS electronic index via eJust portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS corporate index for identical or conflicting names; submit a name reservation request through the eJust portal; obtain a reservation certificate. Reservation grants priority for one month, renewable once.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Passport copy / eID of the applying general partner
Declaration of proposed corporate purpose (ISIC 3250 manufacture of absorbable surgical sutures)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused due to conflict or protected trademark, select a new distinctive name and re-submit; contest the refusal before the competent District Court chamber within statutory deadlines.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the limited partnership agreement (articles of association)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (recommended for notarised form) or parties directly under private signature; subsequent registration duty at AEDT
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Limited Partnership Agreement in one original (notarial deed or private act) containing the corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose (manufacture of absorbable polyglycolic acid braided sutures), term, capital contribution schedule, rights of limited partners, powers of the general partner and manager, and transfer rules. Obtain specimen signatures of the manager and each founding partner.
required_dossiers: Draft limited partnership agreement
Certified passport copies of all founding partners
Proof of residential address of each partner
Non-disqualification declaration of the proposed manager
Subscription schedule evidencing capital contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any defect is cured by an amending addendum (avenant) executed in the same form as the original deed; if the deed was notarised, rectification is performed with the same notary before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers, via the eJust portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Electronically file the constitutional deed and statutory particulars (name, legal form 'SCSp', registered office, partners, manager, contributions) through eJust; pay the EUR 53.30 filing fee; the RCS issues a certificate of registration and the filing is published in the RESA, giving legal effect toward third parties.
required_dossiers: Notarised or originally executed partnership deed
Form – request for registration (eJust)
Declaration of acceptance of office by the manager
Power of attorney if filing through counsel
Proof of payment of the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query, submit a rectification or missing particulars within 15 days; an express refusal may be challenged before the commercial chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement within the period indicated by the RCS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fiscal registrations – VAT (TVA), direct tax file, and municipal business declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); commune of the registered office via guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the VAT start-of-activity declaration on guichet.lu; file the partnership deed with the ACD for tax-file setup (the SCSp is fiscally transparent and profit is taxed at partner level); lodge the municipal business declaration ('déclaration d'exploitation') with the commune for the local trade tax (taxe professionnelle communale).
required_dossiers: RCS extract / certificate of registration
Limited partnership agreement
Passport copies of all partners
Description of the manufacturing activity and expected turnover
Bank account details (IBAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend and resubmit the registration forms via guichet.lu if rejected; if the tax-transparent status is disputed, request a formal tax ruling from the ACD (service des rulings) before closing the first accounting period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and environmental licensing – classified establishment and environmental notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'environnement (AEV); Commission des établissements classés; Ministry of the Economy – Industry Directorate; local commune building authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the 'établissement classé' application under the Luxembourg Law of 15 July 2022 on classified establishments, including site and building plans, the production process flow (braiding, coating, heat-setting, cleaning, sterilization), wastewater and waste-management plans, solvent emission inventory, and fire safety concept. Obtain the operating authorization before commissioning production. An environmental incidence notice (notice d'évaluation des incidences) is required due to the chemical and water-use aspects of suture manufacturing.
required_dossiers: Classified establishment application form (AEV)
Site and building plans
Process description covering ISIC 3250 surgical suture assembly
Material Safety Data Sheets for polyglycolic acid, solvents, and lubricants
Wastewater discharge compliance statement
Waste management and sterilization residue (EtO) plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is incomplete, AEV issues a formal notice listing missing items; applicant supplements the file within the prescribed delay. Negative decisions or unfavourable opinions of the Commission des établissements classés may be cured by amended process designs and appealed before the administrative courts within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Medical device manufacturing registration and occupational / fire clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de la Santé – Direction de la Santé (Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Luxembourg manufacturer and manufacturing site in EUDAMED under Medical Device Regulation (EU) 2017/745; maintain an ISO 13485 quality management system and CE-marked absorbable PGA sutures; obtain the ITM workplace health-and-safety file approval and the CGDIS fire safety certificate; complete the municipal building and structural completion inspection before production.
required_dossiers: Manufacturer registration form (EUDAMED)
ISO 13485 quality management certificate
Technical documentation for absorbable polyglycolic acid braided sutures
Fire safety and evacuation plan approved by CGDIS
ITM occupational health and safety assessment file
Municipal building completion and structural inspection certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address ITM and CGDIS observations through a corrective action plan and re-inspection; for EUDAMED deficiencies, amend the technical file and re-submit; if the CE marking route is disputed, engage a notified body consultation with the Direction de la Santé's medical devices unit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) – Direction de l'industrie, in conjunction with the Administration de l'environnement and the Commission des établissements classés
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'exploitation d'un établissement classé (Classified Establishment Operating Authorization) under the Law of 15 July 2022, together with the EU medical device manufacturing registration under Regulation (EU) 2017/745

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Authority), Ministry of Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Controlled establishment – registration tier (class 3) with an environmental incidence notice; full EIA report is not required at the planned production scale, but is triggered if wastewater discharge exceeds 50 m³/day or if Annex I thresholds for chemical effluent treatment are crossed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to municipal sewer: pH 6–9.5; BOD5 ≤ 500 mg/L; COD ≤ 1,000 mg/L; TSS ≤ 600 mg/L. Solvent and VOC emissions comply with EU Solvent Emissions Directive limits; EtO sterilization workplace exposure ≤ 0.1 mg/m³; hazardous and medical waste segregated and disposed under Luxembourg waste regulations; finished device residuals meet ISO 10993-7 limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the CGDIS covering evacuation routes, fire-resistance rating, and extinguishing systems; ITM occupational clearance for cleanroom ventilation (ISO 14644), chemical storage, and machine guarding; municipal structural completion and building-use certificate prior to commissioning production lines.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; taxpayer portal: MyGuichet.lu and https://pfs.guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an SCSp, register the limited partnership deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) to obtain the statutory 13-digit matricule number. Apply to AEDT for VAT identification using the applicable VAT registration application (Form 160 or electronic filing through MyGuichet); non-resident applicants without a permanent establishment may be required to appoint a tax representative in Luxembourg. The SCSp is treated as a separate taxable person for VAT purposes despite its income-tax transparency.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists in Luxembourg. An SCSp is fiscally transparent by statutory default for direct income and net wealth tax purposes. No election is available to treat a properly constituted SCSp as fully opaque; however, Luxembourg's anti-hybrid and ATAD rules may recharacterize tax treatment in cross-border securities or financing structures to prevent double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Value Added Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover threshold for established Luxembourg taxable persons; non-established foreign suppliers have no threshold and must register from the first taxable supply in Luxembourg. Intra-Community distance sales and cross-border digital services to Luxembourg consumers may trigger registration at the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold or, where applicable, the Luxembourg domestic EUR 35,000 threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate real-time transaction-by-transaction fiscal clearance or mandatory B2B electronic invoicing for private-sector supplies. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for business-to-government (B2G) transactions using PEPPOL/FACTUR-X format. VAT compliance is based on periodic VAT returns and, for eligible taxpayers, submission of the Luxembourg SAF-T (Standard Audit File for Taxes) in XML. No digital stamping or real-time national clearance system is in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods that are physically dispatched or transported by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf to a destination outside the EU qualify for the 0% VAT export exemption under Luxembourg VAT law. The supplier must obtain and retain documentary evidence that the goods left the EU, such as a valid customs export declaration, transport documentation, and commercial evidence identifying the foreign customer and destination. Certain services directly connected with exported goods or services consumed outside the EU may also be zero-rated with equivalent evidentiary support.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The 0% export exemption is presumptive and subject to post-clearance audits by AEDT. If the mandatory documentation bundle is incomplete, unreliable, or not timely retained, the supply is recharacterized as a Luxembourg domestic supply and VAT at 17% must be clawed back, together with default interest of 0.75% per month (or the statutory rate in force). Administrative penalties may reach 50% of the tax shortfall for negligence or intentional concealment; fraudulent export schemes are criminally prosecuted and carry additional fines and imprisonment. The ordinary reassessment period is five years, extended to ten years for fraud-related cases. Where export zero-rating is denied, supplier's corresponding input VAT deductions are likewise disallowed, amplifying the total financial exposure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking supervision, FX licensing, and cross-border payment infrastructure oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg has full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions under Articles 63–66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). No exchange control approvals are required for capital contributions, profit repatriation, or trade-related remittances. SCSp profit distribution follows the partnership agreement and is tax-transparent; remittance is subject only to standard anti-money-laundering and tax compliance checks, not foreign exchange authorisation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds, no minimum conversion ratio, and no forced repatriation timeline. Export receipts may be held in any freely convertible currency in Luxembourg or foreign accounts, subject to standard bank reporting thresholds and CSSF record-keeping obligations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for fully offshore digital EMI providers. Luxembourg-recognised electronic money institutions (PSD2-licensed via CSSF) can offer virtual IBANs and cross-border clearing, but an SCSp engaged in surgical consumables manufacturing requires a full corporate current account with structured trade finance capabilities (SWIFT MT103, LC issuance), which most EMIs do not provide. Any EMI used must hold a valid EU passport and maintain a physical Luxembourg or EU registration, otherwise onboarding is rejected under CSSF outsourcing rules.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted for low-risk corporate clients with complete notarised documentation and digital identity verification, but in practice Luxembourg credit institutions require at least one physical meeting with the general partner or authorised signatory for a partnership structure like an SCSp. For the surgical suture needle assembly scope, an on-site KYC interview at the bank's Luxembourg office is strongly recommended to satisfy the CSSF's senior management responsibility and avoid account onboarding rejection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-tier ownership with an SCSp general partner that is itself a Luxembourg corporate vehicle
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the RCS registration for the SCSp and general partner; full register of beneficial owners (RBE) extract; notarised partnership agreement; signed investment consent; organisational chart detailing the economic chain; source of funds declaration signed by all ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medical-device manufacturing classification (ISIC 3250) raising enhanced due diligence on product compliance and trade counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid Ministry of Health establishment licence; CE marking certificates for surgical sutures; ISO 13485 certification; audited financial statements; list of target wholesale buyers and distribution contracts; evidence of compliance with MDR 2017/745 where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high transaction throughput for supplier payments and capital account movements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed 12-month cash flow projection; complete list of known suppliers with jurisdiction and beneficial ownership; purchase orders and pro-forma invoices; treasury control policy describing separation of duties; confirmation that no sanctions-related jurisdictions are involved.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing uses SWIFT MT103 from the ultimate shareholder bank account to the SCSp operational account at the Luxembourg bank. The remittance information field must explicitly state 'SCSp Capital Contribution – Restricted Capital Account' and use ISO 20022 external purpose code INTC (intercompany transaction) or equivalent. For contributions above EUR 100,000, the receiving Luxembourg bank will perform standard source of funds documentation and report the transaction to established statistical systems; no prior central bank approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for raw material procurement and finished goods distribution are executed through (a) SWIFT MT103 direct transfer for open-account deliveries, (b) Commercial Letters of Credit under ICC UCP600 for documentary collections, and (c) SWIFT MT700/MT707 for import/export LCs. Payments to EU suppliers in EUR may be settled via SEPA direct credit. A full audit trail is maintained in the treasury management system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/GBP) quoted on the interbank market with maturities up to 12 months
FX swaps (EUR against USD or CNY) for working capital liquidity management
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY) permitted with a licensed Luxembourg credit institution

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to currencies with offshore restriction on deliverability (e.g., INR, IDR) where the reference rate is published by the ECB or an authorised benchmark administrator

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS Annual Data Confirmation (Confirmation annuelle des informations au RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one calendar month following the anniversary of the RCS registration date of the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted confirmation attracts administrative fines of up to EUR 1,000; persistent non-compliance for two consecutive annual cycles allows the RCS to initiate administrative strike-off of the registration file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Dépôt des comptes annuels et autres pièces)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial-year close; for a calendar-year SCSp, the deposit must be completed by 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit is punishable by fines up to EUR 1,250 and a formal order from the Public Prosecutor's Office; continuing default over two years may result in administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Register Compliance (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Where a qualifying ownership or control change occurs, an updated UBO declaration must be filed within one month of the event; the general partner must confirm the in-house UBO register accuracy no later than the approval date of the annual accounts.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure or delay in declaring beneficial owners can give rise to criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment; the RBE may publish the non-compliance on the public file and restrict proof of legal standing; repeated annual confirmation default may contribute to RCS administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is compulsory for the SCSp when it exceeds two of the three Luxembourg small-undertaking thresholds: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, average workforce above 50 employees; audit may also be required by the partnership agreement, by member vote, or by CSSF regulation for regulated funds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts of commercial and partnership companies, implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is permitted for unlisted undertakings and is mandatory for public-interest entities and certain regulated financial undertakings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019, the SCSp must maintain a complete and accurate UBO register and file all qualifying ownership changes with the RBE within one month; no separate annual public UBO renewal filing is required absent a change, but the general partner must perform an annual confirmation of the local UBO register at the annual accounts approval cycle and file an RBE update within one month of every transfer of partnership interests.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% for a fully taxable Luxembourg corporate entity (15% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax in Luxembourg City). A Luxembourg SCSp is fiscally transparent and has no entity-level corporate income tax liability; profits and losses pass through to its partners.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The SCSp itself is subject to 0% Luxembourg corporate income tax, 0% municipal business tax and 0% net wealth tax because of fiscal transparency. Qualifying partners may use the Luxembourg participation exemption (80% exemption on dividends and capital gains) if the partner is a Luxembourg corporate taxpayer holding at least 10% or a minimum acquisition price; an industrial partner carrying out an actual Luxembourg manufacturing activity of surgical suture needles may benefit from ordinary business expense deduction, investment tax credits and R&D tax treatment for qualifying manufacturing intangibles.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Luxembourg Partnership Income Tax Declaration (annual informational return for fiscally transparent partnerships) filed through the Luxembourg ACD e-Tax portal at guichet.lu; where a non-resident partner has a Luxembourg permanent establishment, that partner may also be separately assessed using the corporate/individual tax return forms.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned to the partnership's accounting year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, the statutory default falls on 31 December of the next year unless an extension is granted by the Luxembourg direct tax administration. Filing demand letters commonly require earlier filing by 31 May for calendar-year taxpayers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp legal name, RCS Luxembourg number, address, fiscal matricule, partnership agreement reference and NACE/ISIC code 3250.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Luxembourg tax identification number and, for any foreign partner, the foreign tax identification number and country of residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description of commercial activity: manufacturing of absorbable polyglycolic acid braided sutures and assembly of surgical suture needles; indication of operating premises and workforce in Luxembourg.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner must confirm whether a permanent establishment exists in Luxembourg; sales invoicing performed through a Luxembourg SCSp with local employees and decision-making will normally trigger a Luxembourg taxable permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C (Taxable Profit or Loss Allocation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of the commercial/taxable profit or loss of the SCSp after arm-length adjustments, with the share attributable to each partner set out on the schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident partner, allocate only the Luxembourg-source industrial and commercial profit attributable to the Luxembourg permanent establishment; attach the partner's tax residence certificate and treaty article claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of intercompany transactions: purchases of polyglycolic acid raw materials, suture needle components, toll manufacturing fees, management charges, royalties, interest and disposal of manufacturing intangibles.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should submit the group master file and Luxembourg local file references, including transfer pricing policies for the toll assembly arrangement and benchmarking documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of personnel count, payroll, physical office/production space, local decision-making, bank accounts and operational expenditure in Luxembourg.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the non-resident partner is not claiming treaty benefits unless the SCSp is supported by real business presence; a purely passive SCSp cannot access beneficial ownership protections under Luxembourg tax treaties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative penalty of approximately EUR 250 to EUR 2,500; if tax is assessed after failure to file, a 10% penalty surcharge is imposed; default interest accrues monthly at 0.8% on the tax due; continued non-compliance enables daily coercive fines and tax collection by seizure.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Distributions or profit withdrawals from an SCSp do not carry Luxembourg dividend withholding tax because the SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not the payer of a dividend. If a Luxembourg resident company were the dividend payer instead, the statutory Luxembourg domestic dividend withholding tax is 15%, reduced to 0% under the Luxembourg parent-subsidiary participation regime where conditions of minimum holding period and shareholding are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For SCSp profit withdrawals, no Luxembourg withholding tax is normally levied, so treaty relief and TRC submission are unnecessary at the partnership level. Where a Luxembourg corporate payer has withheld tax, or where a non-resident partner's Luxembourg permanent establishment is assessed on profits, the beneficial owner must obtain a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) from the partner's residence country and file a Luxembourg withholding tax reclaim or treaty exemption (including the appropriate ACD form) before the expiry of the statutory limitation period; the tax treaty article must be invoked and beneficial ownership/professional/economic substance evidence attached.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose domestic withholding tax on outbound interest or royalty payments; the statutory domestic rate is 0%. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive provides an additional 0% rate for qualifying EU related corporate payers/beneficial owners; tax treaties may reduce residual rates, and classic Luxembourg treaty policy provides 0% on interest and 0% to 10% on royalties depending on the specific DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg has no broad statutory monetary threshold for contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, but the ACD expects a local file for cross-border related-party transactions exceeding EUR 100,000 per category; a master file is required in practice when the multinational group has consolidated turnover of at least EUR 50,000,000; country-by-country reporting obligation starts at consolidated group revenue of EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg is a unitary national tax jurisdiction, and no separate sub-state Economic Substance Regulations apply as in certain Crown Dependencies. However, Luxembourg's general anti-abuse rule, OECD substance-over-form rules, EU ATAD principles and bilateral tax treaty beneficial ownership requirements require the SCSp to maintain real substance: qualified staff in Luxembourg premises, local management, operating expenditure, commercial risk and independent decision-making for surgical suture manufacturing operations. A SCSp used only as a conduit for profit stripping will be recharacterised and denied treaty access.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting Luxembourg-source manufacturing profit from the SCSp tax return, inflating deductible management fees, or allocating profit to a non-resident partner with no permanent establishment while the manufacturing activity is actually carried on in Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full understated tax with penalty surcharge up to 100% of the evaded tax; default interest at 0.8% per month; criminal fine of up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment of up to 2 years for intentional tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner of the SCSp and, if the general partner is corporate, its directors/managers who sign or knowingly cause a false declaration are jointly and severally liable for restitution of evaded tax; courts may lift the corporate veil for abuse of the corporate form, with personal asset recovery, travel restrictions and disqualification from management following criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Thin Capitalisation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an artificially low cost-plus return on the Luxembourg toll manufacturing entity, charging excessive royalties or interest to the Luxembourg SCSp, or injecting debt in place of true equity without arm-length conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment increasing the Luxembourg taxable base; disallowance of excessive interest; late payment interest at 0.8% per month; penalty of up to 10% of the under-declared tax; administrative fines for failure to produce contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner and the local manager may be personally assessed for penalties if the deficient policy was knowingly advanced; tax administrations may pierce the partnership structure and recover under-declared tax from the general partner as an unlimited partner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp as a letterbox without employees, premises, bank activity or commercial substance; using the partnership merely to insert a tax-favourable jurisdiction into the multinational surgical suture supply chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty benefits; recharacterisation of the SCSp as a fully taxable Luxembourg entity; substitution of taxable base by anti-abuse assessment; removal from the commercial register and administrative dissolution for persistent lack of substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors or others acting through the shell may be personally liable for unpaid taxes as de facto managers; travel bans, asset freezes and director disqualification apply where a significant tax debt is linked to abstract use of a shell vehicle.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain and file the Luxembourg register of beneficial owners (RBE) for the SCSp; failure to conduct customer due diligence on partners or to file suspicious transaction reports on Swift/telegraphic wire payments related to suture contract manufacturing proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to EUR 125,000 per violation under Luxembourg AML/RBE law, with repeated or serious violations exposing fines up to EUR 1,000,000; freezing of bank transactions, delayed disbursement and regulatory suspension of the manufacturing licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers and beneficial owners are criminally liable for intentional non-disclosure of beneficial ownership; imprisonment of up to 5 years and personal fines up to EUR 50,000; directors may be barred from holding office and repatriation/profit distribution may be blocked by judicial order.
